jobs.prompt:
test(cpp): compare the native gateway against the current production gateway in the paired conformance suite

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-drift-port-20261119-44456061234-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi. This branch contains only the native C++20 gateway (`cpp/gateway/`) and `static/`. Its paired conformance suite (`cpp/gateway/conformance/`, see `cpp/gateway/README.md` and `cpp/gateway/docs/CLEANUP-PLAN.md`) runs the original TypeScript gateway on Bun next to the native one over local mocks and compares 186 cases. The TypeScript is obtained by `git fetch origin <commit>` + `git worktree add --detach` of the commit in `cpp/gateway/conformance/oracle-revision.txt`, currently a historical commit. Production runs branch `development`, which has since changed; this branch already ported those changes (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-drift-port-20261119.md`: against `development` commit `9353aa20` the native gateway matches on 184 of 186 cases, the other two being known shared validation failures; against the historical pin there are eight expected differences). The pin could not be moved because the gate needs a smoke fixture that `development` does not contain and that report restored in scratch.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit anything outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


OWNED PATHS
- `cpp/gateway/conformance/**`, `cpp/gateway/tests/production_smoke/**`, `cpp/gateway/bench/request_path/**` only as far as the conformance launcher needs, `cpp/gateway/docs/**`, your report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-conformance-pin-20261119.md`.

TASK
Make the committed conformance gate compare against current production: (1) read the drift report to see exactly which fixture or launcher file the gate loads from the oracle checkout and `development` lacks; carry what is needed inside `cpp/gateway/conformance/` (or the existing production_smoke directory) so the gate depends on the oracle checkout only for the TypeScript application itself (`serve.ts`, `src/`, `lib/`, its lockfile); (2) set `oracle-revision.txt` to the exact current `origin/development` commit you verified (full hash) and update every document that cites the pin; (3) run `bash cpp/gateway/conformance/run.sh ...` exactly as the README documents, from a clean state, against a package built from your branch (the README and CLEANUP-PLAN give the commands; Docker is available on your runner): the result must be the two known shared failures (`chat-invalid-role`, `responses-invalid-tool-type`) and no other difference. If any other case differs, do NOT change expectations: report the case, both outputs and which side changed. (4) Document in `cpp/gateway/conformance/README.md` (create it if missing) the one command to re-run the gate and the procedure for moving the pin when production changes again. Commit after each step; your process can be restarted without warning.

DONE WHEN
The documented gate passes against the pinned `development` commit with exactly the two known shared failures, from a clean checkout, and the pin, documents and report agree.
